mainTopic: Yoma 44b: The holiness of the area between the אולם and the מזבח, and the differences in the coal pan (מחתה) on יום כיפור
overview: This amud finishes the גמרא's discussion of the levels of holiness (מעלות) in the בית המקדש. רבא explains that all the differences in stepping away (פרישה) between the היכל and the area between the אולם and the מזבח count as one מעלה. A ברייתא adds that people also step away during the inner blood service of certain sacrifices, and רבי פדת gives the source: a גזירה שוה of 'כפרה' from יום הכיפורים. רב אחא בר אהבה tries to prove that the מעלות are דאורייתא, and רבא tries to prove that the אולם shares the holiness of the היכל. The גמרא pushes both proofs aside. The גמרא then turns back to the משנה about the coal pan (מחתה). On regular days a silver pan was used to save money, but on יום כיפור a single gold pan was used to spare the weak כהן גדול. Two answers explain a ברייתא that says two קבין of coals spilled. The amud then lists how the יום כיפור pan was built differently, and רב חסדא begins explaining seven kinds of gold, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the answer: between the אולם and the מזבח only during the קטורת
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of the previous answer: from the area between the אולם and the מזבח, people step away only while the קטורת is being burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...except during the burning of the incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the answer it gave on the previous amud. People only have to leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח while the קטורת is burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full answer contrasts two areas. People must leave the היכל at many times, but they leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח only during הקטרה. That contrast is the מעלה that makes the היכל holier.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning (here, of the קטורת, the incense)
A higher level of holiness, a stricter standard

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the last words of a sentence that started on the previous amud, so read it as the end of the previous answer.

phrases.english: except during the time of the incense burning.
phrases.notes: This finishes the answer about when people stepped away from the area between the אולם and the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁעַת הַקְטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer on the previous amud boundary.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מעלה of the היכל: people step away from it at more times, while from between the אולם and the מזבח they step away only during הקטרה.

steps.title: There is another difference between the two areas
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: there is a second difference. People leave the היכל both for its own service and for the service of קודש הקדשים, but they leave the area between the אולם and the מזבח only for the היכל's service.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also this higher standard. From the היכל, people step away both during its own holy service and during the service of the innermost chamber. From the area between the אולם and the מזבח, they step away only during the service of the היכל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the answer missed a second difference between the two areas. So why speak of only one מעלה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 gave one difference, which was about timing. This step points to another difference: which services require stepping away. The היכל is cleared for its own service and for the service of קודש הקדשים, while the area between the אולם and the מזבח is cleared only for the היכל's service. That means there should be two מעלות, not one.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the main inner hall of the Temple
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל

phrases.english: But there is this higher standard too:
that whereas from the Sanctuary they step away
both during its own holy service,
phrases.notes: For example, blood sprinklings done in the היכל.

phrases.english: and during the holy service of the innermost chamber,
while from between the Entrance Hall and the Altar
they step away only during the holy service of the Sanctuary!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא הָא מַעֲלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that there is only one מעלה between the two areas.
steps.kashyaTarget: The presentation of a single מעלה distinguishing the היכל from the area between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a second difference, about which services require stepping away. So there should be two מעלות counted, not one.

steps.title: רבא: It is all one category of stepping away
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that all these differences belong to one category, פרישה (stepping away), so they count as one מעלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is one category of stepping away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. Every difference mentioned is about the same thing, stepping away, so together they count as one מעלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that there are several details. He groups them together because they are all about the same law, פרישה. So counting them as one מעלה is correct.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is one category of stepping away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שֵׁם פְּרִישָׁה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grouping several details into one category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each difference between the areas should count as a separate מעלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the differences are about פרישה, so they count as one מעלה.
steps.whatToRemember: The היכל is stricter than the area between the אולם and the מזבח in several ways about stepping away. All of these count as one מעלה, because they share the single category of פרישה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: Stepping away also during certain inner sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: just as people step away during the קטורת, they also step away during the blood service of the פר כהן משיח, the פר העלם דבר של צבור, and the שעירי עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: In the same way, people step away during the blood service of the bull of the anointed כהן, the bull for a mistaken ruling of the community, and the goats offered for עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא it is studying and quotes another line from it. This sets up the next question: where does this rule come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, stepping away from the area between the אולם and the מזבח was linked to the קטורת. Here the ברייתא adds three sacrifices whose blood is sprinkled inside the היכל. During their blood service, people must also clear that area.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought by the כהן גדול for a sin done by mistake
The bull brought when the בית דין ruled wrongly and the community sinned
The goats brought for the community's mistaken sin of idol worship

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ פּוֹרְשִׁין בִּשְׁעַת מַתַּן פַּר כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ,
phrases.english: So too they step away during the blood service of the bull of the anointed priest,
and the bull for the community's mistaken ruling,
and the goats for idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: כָּךְ פּוֹרְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to analyze its next clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People step away from the area between the אולם and the מזבח during the blood service of the פר כהן משיח, the פר העלם דבר של צבור, and the שעירי עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just quoted. This sets up רבי פדת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of stepping away is stated in the Torah only for יום הכיפורים. So the גמרא wants to know how it reaches these other sacrifices.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for stepping away during the blood service of these three sacrifices.

steps.title: רבי פדת: A גזירה שוה from יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי פדת derives the rule through a גזירה שוה. The word 'כפרה' appears both for these sacrifices and for the יום הכיפורים service.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פדת said: It is learned from the word 'atonement' here and the word 'atonement' said about יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי פדת gives the source: a word-link (גזירה שוה) between these sacrifices and יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the Torah says no person may be in the אהל מועד while the כהן גדול is making כפרה. These three sacrifices are also described with the word 'כפרה'. The shared word carries the stepping-away rule over to them.

keyTerms.meaning: A derivation from the same word appearing in two places

phrases.english: Rabbi Pedat said:
It is derived from 'atonement' and 'atonement' from Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word 'atonement' shows up in both places, so we learn one from the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי פְּדָת: אָתְיָא כַּפָּרָה כַּפָּרָה מִיּוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'כפרה' from יום הכיפורים, where the Torah requires everyone to leave during the service.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא extends stepping away even to the area between the אולם and the מזבח, which the יום הכיפורים verse does not mention. The next step asks whether that extra boundary is Torah law or a rabbinic safeguard.

steps.title: רב אחא בר אהבה: The levels of holiness are Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אהבה concludes that the מעלות of the Temple are דאורייתא, and that the חכמים received them as a tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר אהבה said: Learn from this that the levels of holiness are from the Torah, and this is how they were received as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר אהבה draws a conclusion from רבי פדת's Torah source. The Temple's levels of holiness are Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יום הכיפורים verse only clears the אהל מועד (the היכל). Yet the ברייתא requires stepping away even from the area between the אולם and the מזבח. רב אחא בר אהבה infers that this extra boundary is not a rabbinic invention: it is דאורייתא, known through a received tradition ('הכי גמירי להו'). Step 8 gives his reasoning, and step 9 rejects it.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned them as a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: רב אחא בר אהבה proposes that the מעלות of the בית המקדש, such as stepping away from between the אולם and the מזבח, are דאורייתא by tradition. Watch step 9, where the גמרא shows his proof is not compelling.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ahava said:
Learn from this: the higher standards are Torah law,
and this is how they learned them by tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַהֲבָה, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מַעֲלוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broader conclusion from רבי פדת's Torah derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Proposed (and later rejected in step 9): the מעלות of holiness in the Temple are דאורייתא, received by the חכמים as a tradition.

steps.title: רב אחא בר אהבה's proof that the stepping-away rule is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר אהבה proves the rule is דאורייתא. If it were only a rabbinic safeguard, people should step away from the whole עזרה, not just from the area between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you thought the rule was rabbinic, why is the area between the אולם and the מזבח special? Is it because people might accidentally wander in? Then they should also step away from the whole עזרה, since there too they might accidentally wander in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רב אחא בר אהבה said the מעלות are דאורייתא. It points out that a rabbinic rule would not stop exactly at the area between the אולם and the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic rule here would be a safeguard, a 'fence' so that people do not accidentally walk into the היכל while the קטורת is burning. But a fence like that should cover the whole עזרה, since anyone in the עזרה could wander in. The rule covers only the strip between the אולם and the מזבח, so it looks like a fixed Torah boundary and not a protective fence.

keyTerms.meaning: Because if you would think (a way of testing an idea by showing where it leads)
From the Rabbis (a rabbinic law, not a Torah law)
The area between the Entrance Hall and the outer altar
They might happen to enter (by accident)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new speaker. It is the reasoning behind רב אחא בר אהבה's conclusion from the previous step.

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind that it is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is trying out the opposite view to see if it holds up.

phrases.english: what is different about the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar?
Is it because perhaps they will happen to enter?
phrases.notes: This would be the reason the רבנן made such a rule.

phrases.english: Then they should also step away from the whole courtyard,
since perhaps they will happen to enter!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּרַבָּנַן, מַאי שְׁנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the conclusion in step 7
steps.raayaObject: That the מעלות (the stepping-away rule) are דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule is limited to the area between the אולם and the מזבח, which does not fit a rabbinic safeguard

steps.title: The area right in front of the Entrance Hall is easy to confuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A rabbinic rule could reasonably cover only the area between the אולם and the מזבח, because nothing separates it from the היכל. The rest of the עזרה is clearly separated by the outer מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between the אולם and the מזבח, nothing separates it from the inside, so the difference is not noticeable. In the rest of the עזרה, the outer מזבח stands in between, so the difference is noticeable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רב אחא בר אהבה's proof. It shows that a rabbinic rule could still make sense even though it covers only one small area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that a rabbinic fence would have to cover the whole עזרה. The גמרא answers that the fence goes only where mistakes are likely. Standing right in front of the אולם, a person could easily drift inside, but the outer מזבח acts as a clear visual barrier for everyone further out. So the limited area no longer proves the rule is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is noticeable (the boundary is clear)
The outer altar, in the courtyard

phrases.english: Between the Entrance Hall and the altar,
since nothing separates it,
the distinction is not noticeable.
The courtyard, since there is
the outer altar that separates,
the distinction is noticeable.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מַפְסֵיק מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove that the rule is rabbinic; it shows the rule could be rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed a rabbinic fence must cover the whole עזרה. In fact, a fence is placed only where mistakes are likely, and the outer מזבח prevents mistakes everywhere else.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once the area between the אולם and the מזבח is treated as a rabbinic fence, רבא can build his next inference on it.

steps.title: רבא: the Entrance Hall and the Sanctuary share one holiness
steps.stepSummary: רבא infers that the אולם and the היכל have one holiness. Otherwise, the ban on the אולם would itself be a גזירה, and the ban on the area in front of it would be a 'גזירה to protect a גזירה', which the חכמים do not make.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn from this that the holiness of the אולם and the היכל is one thing. Because if you thought they were two separate holinesses, the ban on the אולם itself would be a rabbinic decree. Would we then go and make a decree to protect a decree?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds on the idea that the ban between the אולם and the מזבח is a rabbinic fence. From that, he draws a new conclusion about how holy the אולם is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids being in the היכל while the קטורת is offered. If the אולם were a separate, lower holiness, the ban on the אולם would be only rabbinic. The ban on the area in front of the אולם would then be a second rabbinic layer on top of the first. Since the חכמים do not stack decrees like that, the אולם must share the היכל's holiness, so its ban is from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building, where the קטורת is offered
A decree to protect another decree, which the חכמים normally do not make

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the אולם (the Entrance Hall itself) with 'between the אולם and the מזבח' (the open courtyard space in front of it). They are two different places.

phrases.english: Rava said: Learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: קְדוּשַּׁת אוּלָם וְהֵיכָל חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא.
phrases.english: the sanctity of the Entrance Hall and the Sanctuary is one matter.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: For if you thought they were two separate sanctities,
the Entrance Hall itself would be a decree,
and will we arise and issue a decree for a decree?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses step 9's view that the area in front of the אולם is a rabbinic fence to draw a new inference about the אולם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אולם and the היכל share one level of holiness, so the Torah's ban on the היכל applies to the אולם too.

steps.title: The Entrance Hall and the space in front of it form one unit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's inference. The אולם and the area in front of it share one holiness, so a single גזירה covers both, even if the היכל and the אולם are two separate holinesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The אולם and the area between the אולם and the מזבח are one holiness. The היכל and the אולם are two holinesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. It shows his inference does not have to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's argument depended on the ban in front of the אולם being a second, separate layer. The גמרא says the אולם and the area in front of it are one holiness, so the חכמים made one single גזירה covering both together. That means there is no 'גזירה for a גזירה', and the היכל and the אולם can still be two different holinesses.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא leaves open both whether the stepping-away rule is דאורייתא and whether the אולם shares the היכל's holiness. Each proof was pushed aside: the outer מזבח explains why the rule is limited to one area, and grouping the אולם with the space in front of it avoids a 'גזירה for a גזירה'.

phrases.english: No, the Entrance Hall and the area between the Entrance Hall and the altar
are one sanctity,
while the Sanctuary and the Entrance Hall are two sanctities.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אוּלָם וּבֵין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ חֲדָא קְדוּשָּׁה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's inference from step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's proof. It does not prove that the היכל and the אולם differ; it shows they could.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed the ban in front of the אולם was a separate second decree. In fact, the אולם and the area in front of it can be grouped as one holiness under one decree.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither inference is forced. The holiness of the אולם relative to the היכל remains unproven.

steps.title: Why use a silver pan on regular days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about the silver coal pan on regular days and asks why a silver pan was used for scooping.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on every other day, the כהן would scoop coals with a silver pan, and so on. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה and asks a simple 'why' question. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ordinary days the כהן scooped the coals with a silver מחתה and then poured them into a gold one. The obvious question is why he didn't simply scoop with the gold pan from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Coal pan / fire pan used to carry coals

phrases.english: On every day he would scoop up the coals
with a pan of silver, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line: he then poured the coals into a gold pan

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of the אולם's holiness to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a silver pan, rather than the gold one, was used to scoop the coals on regular days.

steps.title: The Torah protects Jewish money
steps.stepSummary: Scooping hot coals wears down a pan, so the cheaper silver pan was used to avoid ruining the expensive gold one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spared the money of the Jewish people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a silver pan was used to save money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scraping coals off the altar wears down the pan. Using silver for that rough job keeps the costly gold pan from wearing out, and that protects the community's funds.

keyTerms.term: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: The Torah cares about (spares) the money of the Jewish people

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known principle that appears in several places in ש״ס: even in the בית המקדש, the Torah avoids needless waste of Jewish money.

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: The Torah spared the money of the Jewish people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Silver was used to save the gold pan from wear, because the Torah spares Jewish money.

steps.title: Why only one gold pan on יום כיפור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that on יום כיפור the כהן גדול scooped with a gold pan and brought that same pan inside, and asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but today (יום כיפור), he scoops with a gold pan, and with it he brings the coals in. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks why יום כיפור is different. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the money-saving switch from silver to gold is skipped. The כהן גדול scoops with the gold pan and carries that same pan into קודש הקדשים, so the גמרא wants to know why the usual practice was dropped.

phrases.english: But today he scoops with a pan of gold,
and with it he would bring the coals in.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹם חוֹתֶה בְּשֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the money-saving practice of step 13 is not followed on יום כיפור.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the כהן גדול uses a single gold pan on יום כיפור instead of switching pans.

steps.title: To spare the weakened כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: Because the כהן גדול is weak from fasting and from doing all the service alone, he is spared the extra work of switching pans.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the weakness of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the כהן גדול is weak on יום כיפור, so his work is made lighter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור the כהן גדול fasts and does the whole service himself. Pouring coals from one pan into another would be an extra tiring task. Here, concern for his strength comes before saving money.

phrases.english: Because of the weakness of the High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One pan is used to save the fasting כהן גדול from the effort of switching pans.

steps.title: One קב of coals spilled while pouring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about pan sizes (scoop with four קבין, pour into three) and brings a teaching that the extra קב that spilled was swept into the canal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on every day, with a pan of four קבין, and so on. It was taught: a קב of coals was scattered, and he would sweep them into the canal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה about pan sizes and adds a teaching about what happened to the coals that did not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the כהן scooped with a pan holding four קבין and poured the coals into one holding three. So one קב could not fit and spilled. The teaching says the כהן swept those spilled coals into the אמה, the water channel in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of volume (a סאה = 6 קבין)
The water canal running through the עזרה

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם בְּשֶׁל אַרְבַּעַת קַבִּין וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: On every day, with a pan of four kav, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: pour into three קבין. רבי יוסי says: scoop with a סאה (six קבין).

phrases.english: It was taught: if a kav of coals was scattered,
he sweeps them into the canal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: נִתְפַּזְּרוּ לוֹ קַב גֶּחָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה, about how big the pans were.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When pouring from the four-קב pan into the three-קב pan, one קב of coals spills and is swept into the אמה.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree on how much spilled
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says one קב spilled, and another ברייתא says two קבין spilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: a קב. And another ברייתא teaches: two קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side that give different amounts of spilled coals. This sets up the problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number that spilled depends on how big the scooping pan was. So each amount should match one of the views in the משנה. The second number, two קבין, is the one that will cause trouble.

phrases.english: One baraita teaches: a kav,
and another baraita teaches: two kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא: קַב, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: קַבַּיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second version of the teaching in step 16 that gives a different number.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two traditions about the spill: one קב, or two קבין.

steps.title: Whose view gives two קבין?
steps.stepSummary: One קב fits the רבנן (4 minus 3), but two קבין fits neither the רבנן nor רבי יוסי (6 minus 3 = 3).
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the ברייתא that says one קב follows the רבנן. But the one that says two קבין, whose view is it? It is not the רבנן and not רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second ברייתא, because its number does not match either view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, four קבין poured into three leaves one extra קב. For רבי יוסי, a סאה (six קבין) poured into three leaves three extra קבין. Two קבין matches neither one, so the גמרא asks who the author of that ברייתא could be.

keyTerms.meaning: A volume of six קבין (רבי יוסי's scooping pan)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי יוסי's view is 'two קבין.' His scooping pan holds a סאה, which is six קבין. Six minus three leaves three קבין spilled, not two.

phrases.english: Granted, this one that teaches one kav follows the Rabbis.
But that one that teaches two kav, whose view is it?
It is neither the Rabbis nor Rabbi Yosei!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָךְ דְּתָנֵי קַב רַבָּנַן, אֶלָּא הָךְ דְּתָנֵי קַבַּיִים מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the math of the משנה's pan sizes to attack the 'two קבין' ברייתא from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that says two קבין of coals spilled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן (4 into 3) give one קב spilled, and רבי יוסי (6 into 3) gives three. Two קבין fits no known view, so the ברייתא seems to have no author.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The two-קב teaching follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the ברייתא saying two קבין spilled follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. He holds that the pan brought inside held only two קבין. So scooping four and bringing in two leaves two spilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: That ברייתא follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל says the כהן גדול brought the coals inside in a pan that held two קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 18 by finding a תנא whose numbers produce exactly two spilled קבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the רבנן, on every other day the כהן scooped with a four-קב pan. רבי ישמעאל agrees about the scooping, but says the pan brought inside held only two קבין, not three. Four minus two leaves two קבין spilled, which matches the second ברייתא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Two קבין (a קב is a unit of volume)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא,
phrases.english: It is the view of Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka,
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא that says two קבין spilled.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
He would bring the coals in with a pan of two kav.
phrases.notes: The scooping pan held four קבין, so two were left over.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by assigning the two-קב ברייתא to a third תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No known opinion produces exactly two spilled קבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל's two-קב inner pan, together with a four-קב scooping pan, leaves two קבין spilled.

steps.title: רב אשי: It can even follow רבי יוסי, using a desert סאה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the two-קב ברייתא can even follow רבי יוסי. The 'סאה' used for scooping was a desert סאה, which equals five Jerusalem קבין. Pouring five into a three-קב pan leaves two spilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: You can even say it follows רבי יוסי. This is what he means: every day the כהן scooped with a pan the size of a desert סאה, and poured the coals into a pan holding three Jerusalem קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second answer that keeps רבי יוסי's numbers, but redefines which measuring system is being used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 assumed a סאה equals six קבין, so 6 − 3 = 3 spilled. רב אשי explains that the סאה here is a desert סאה. Jerusalem measures were larger, so a desert סאה equals only five Jerusalem קבין. Five minus three gives exactly two קבין spilled.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the answer works even according to this view)
A desert סאה, the older and smaller measure (equal to five Jerusalem קבין)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume a סאה always equals six קבין here. The trick is that the סאה and the קבין are measured in two different systems: desert versus Jerusalem.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Yosei,
and this is what he means:
Every day he would scoop
with a pan of a desert se'ah,
phrases.notes: A desert סאה equals five Jerusalem קבין.

phrases.english: and pour into a pan of three Jerusalem kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to step 18, different from רב חסדא's in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's סאה is six of the same קבין, so three would spill.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סאה is a desert סאה equal to five Jerusalem קבין, so two spill.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the 'two קבין' ברייתא. רב חסדא assigns it to רבי ישמעאל (4 − 2). רב אשי keeps רבי יוסי and uses a desert סאה (5 − 3).

steps.title: The משנה: The everyday pan was heavy, the יום כיפור pan light
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: every day the pan was heavy, but on יום כיפור it was light.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day the pan was heavy, but today (יום כיפור) it was light.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about the pan's weight. This sets up the ברייתא and the explanation that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic within the משנה. It is no longer about how many coals there were, but about how the pan itself was built. Like the earlier point about not switching pans, it fits the theme of making the work easier for the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Every day it was heavy,
but today it was light.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה כְּבֵידָה, וְהַיּוֹם קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the volume of coals to the build of the pan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום כיפור pan was lighter than the everyday pan.

steps.title: ברייתא: The יום כיפור pan had thin walls and a long handle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds more differences. The everyday pan had thick walls, but the יום כיפור pan had thin ones. The everyday handle was short, but the יום כיפור handle was long.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Every day its wall was thick, but today it was thin. Every day it was short, but today it was long.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives more details about how the יום כיפור pan was different. This prepares for the question of why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thin walls explain how the pan became light, which is what the משנה said. The long handle is a new detail, and its purpose is about to be explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Its wall or 'skin' (the metal body of the pan)

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה גִּלְדָּהּ עָבֶה,
phrases.english: It was taught: Every day its wall was thick,
but today it was thin.
Every day its handle was short,
but today it was long.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיְתָה גִּלְדָּהּ עָבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the משנה's 'heavy versus light' with more physical details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום כיפור pan had thin walls and a long handle.

steps.title: Why was the handle long?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind these changes, especially the long handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the יום כיפור pan was built this way. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thin wall obviously makes the pan lighter. A longer handle, though, seems to add weight, so the גמרא wants to know what it was for.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's details.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the long handle (and the lighter design).

steps.title: So the כהן גדול can brace the pan on his arm
steps.stepSummary: The long handle let the כהן גדול rest it along his arm. That way his arm helped carry the weight, instead of his hand holding everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that the arm of the כהן גדול could help him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the design helps the weak כהן גדול carry the pan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a long handle, he could lay it along his forearm, so the weight was supported by more than just his grip. This fits the theme from step 15: on יום כיפור the כהן גדול is weak from fasting, so his work is made easier.

phrases.english: So that the arm
of the High Priest would help him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא זְרוֹעוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מְסַיַּיעְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The long handle lets the כהן גדול support the pan on his arm.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a running theme: the יום כיפור vessels were designed to ease the burden on the fasting כהן גדול.

steps.title: ברייתא: On יום כיפור the pan had a ring
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that only on יום כיפור the pan had a ring (ניאשתיק) attached. This is the view of בן הסגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Every day the pan had no ring, but today it had a ring. These are the words of בן הסגן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about a feature added to the יום כיפור pan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ring clattered against the handle and made a sound. ראשונים connect this to the פסוק 'ונשמע קולו בבואו אל הקודש'. This is a new detail about the pan, and it is taught in the name of בן הסגן.

keyTerms.meaning: A ring or loop attached to the handle

steps.whatToRemember: The יום כיפור pan was light, thin-walled, long-handled, and (according to בן הסגן) had a ring. All of these were changes from the everyday pan.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, בְּכׇל יוֹם לֹא הָיָה לָהּ נִיאַשְׁתִּיק,
phrases.english: It was taught: Every day it did not have a ring,
but today it had a ring.
These are the words of the son of the Deputy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, בְּכׇל יוֹם לֹא הָיָה לָהּ נִיאַשְׁתִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another difference between the everyday pan and the יום כיפור pan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן הסגן, the יום כיפור pan had a ring attached.

steps.title: The everyday pan was made of greenish gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on every other day, the pan's gold was greenish.
steps.simpleTranslation: On every day, its gold was greenish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about the pan (מחתה). It says that on a regular day the pan was made of greenish gold. This line sets up the next discussion about different kinds of gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another difference between the everyday pan and the יום כיפור pan, like the weight, walls and handle we saw before. The משנה goes on to say that on יום כיפור the gold was red, which was a finer gold. The word 'greenish' makes us ask what kinds of gold exist, and רב חסדא answers that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Every day, meaning a regular day that is not יום כיפור
Its gold, meaning the gold of the pan
Greenish or yellowish-green. A lower grade of gold

phrases.english: On every day, its gold was greenish.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: but on this day (יום כיפור) it was red.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל יוֹם הָיָה זְהָבָהּ יָרוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of differences between the everyday pan and the יום כיפור pan (weight, walls, handle, ring) with a new difference, the color of its gold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The everyday pan was made of greenish gold. The יום כיפור pan was made of a finer, red gold.

steps.title: רב חסדא lists seven kinds of gold
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says there are seven kinds of gold: gold, good gold, gold of אופיר, מופז gold, שחוט gold, סגור gold and פרוים gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: There are seven kinds of gold: gold, good gold, gold of אופיר, מופז gold, שחוט gold, סגור gold and פרוים gold.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the משנה mentioned different colors of gold, רב חסדא gives a full list of the seven kinds of gold named in תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information. The משנה only spoke about greenish and red gold, but רב חסדא shows that the פסוקים use seven different names for gold. Each name points to a different type or quality, and the גמרא will now explain them one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: שחוט gold, a type named in the פסוקים (explained later in the גמרא)
סגור ('closed') gold, a type named in the פסוקים
פרוים gold, a type named in the פסוקים

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
There are seven kinds of gold:
Gold, and good gold,
and gold of Ophir, and glistening (mufaz) gold,
and shachut gold, and closed (sagur) gold,
and parvayim gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא שִׁבְעָה זְהָבִים הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה's mention of gold colors leads רב חסדא to list all the kinds of gold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are seven kinds of gold named in תנ"ך.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this part of the sugya explains this list, so it is the outline for what comes next.

steps.title: Plain gold versus good gold, proven from a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why 'gold' and 'good gold' are listed separately. The פסוק says 'and the gold of that land is good'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gold and good gold are different, as it is written: 'And the gold of that land is good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining רב חסדא's list. It shows from a פסוק that there is regular gold and also a better 'good' gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in בראשית praises the gold of a certain land as 'good'. That means some gold is better than ordinary gold. So 'gold' and 'good gold' are two separate kinds.

keyTerms.meaning: Good gold, a higher quality than plain gold
As it is written. This introduces a פסוק as a source
That land, the land described in בראשית

phrases.english: Gold and good gold,
as it is written: 'And the gold of that land is good.'
phrases.notes: בראשית ב:יב. Calling it 'good' shows there is a better grade of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָהָב וְזָהָב טוֹב דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the first two items on רב חסדא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Good gold is a separate, higher grade than plain gold, as the פסוק shows.

steps.title: Gold of אופיר comes from אופיר, and the explanation of מופז begins
steps.stepSummary: Gold of אופיר is named after the place it comes from. The גמרא then begins to explain זהב מופז, and that explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gold of אופיר is gold that comes from אופיר. Glistening (מופז) gold is so named...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'gold of אופיר' is simply gold from the place called אופיר. Then it starts explaining the next name, מופז. That explanation finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike 'good gold', which describes quality, this name describes where the gold comes from. The last words open the explanation of זהב מופז, so this step leads straight into the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: Gold of אופיר, gold from the place אופיר
Glistening gold. The גמרא explains this name next

phrases.english: Gold of Ophir is gold that comes from Ophir.
Glistening (mufaz) gold is so named...
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְהַב אוֹפִיר דְּאָתֵי מֵאוֹפִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down רב חסדא's list to the third item and begins the fourth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gold of אופיר is named for where it comes from. The meaning of מופז is about to be explained.
